Today we're going to focus on **Number Properties**, specifically looking at **Odd/Even** constraints and **Absolute Value**. 

This is a super important concept because GRE questions involving absolute values or odd/even variables love to trick you into assuming just one scenario (like assuming variables are always positive). Learning to systematically test different cases—like positive vs. negative—will help you catch hidden outcomes, which is especially crucial for Quantitative Comparison questions!

I feel like testing both equations out with the same sign first and then different signs.

That is exactly the right approach! Testing same signs and different signs is the perfect way to handle absolute value questions, because absolute value behaves differently depending on whether the numbers are working together or working against each other.

Your strategy was perfect. When you test numbers with the same sign (like $x=2$ and $y=3$), both quantities equal 5, which points to C. But when you test numbers with different signs (like $x=2$ and $y=-3$), Quantity A becomes 1 while Quantity B stays 5, pointing to B. Since the relationship changes depending on the numbers you pick, D is the only answer.

Whenever you see absolute values or variables without specified signs in Quantitative Comparison, this "positive vs. negative" testing strategy is your best friend.
